issue_context.title: Unhelpful error: Cannot read properties of null (reading '_rawValidators')
issue_context.body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

forms

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

Error thrown: Cannot read properties of null (reading '_rawValidators')

This does not tell the user where the issue is (what component), nor what the invalid form control name is. There is better handling when production mode is not on, but this doesn't help when we are trying to debug an issue that is in our production environment and do not know how to reproduce the issue.

We log unhandled errors to DataDog and when we get this error, there is pretty much nothing we can do to take action on it or fix it since there is no useful information provided in the stack trace.


### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

https://stackblitz.com/edit/stackblitz-starters-cgg4uh?file=src%2Fapp%2Fforms%2Fforms.component.html

comments:
Looks to have already been reported in the past: https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/48379
But that was closed. I have created a stackblitz to reproduce the issue.

Yes, that is the issue, it throws an error with no information when it hits a form control with the wrong name.

In our case, our form controls are created dynamically from database information. In our crash logs in DataDog, we logged this error, but the problem is that we don't have any information on what form control name was used, what part of our application the user was in, etc. Unfortunately this means that we cannot fix the problem without more information.

Here is a link to the diagnostic error that is only thrown in dev mode:
https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/d73a3741a2a49be0ff1710666682c1cf4ae5d701/packages/forms/src/directives/shared.ts#L70

Oh I see, one of the problem is that we strip error messages in prod builds and only log the error code so that wouldn't help you very much. 
We only log issue in error mode to keep the prod bundle as small as possible.

Yes, that is it. It isn't an Angular bug, I'm just requesting aid in finding the source of the problem when the issue occurs. It would be extremely helpful to know the component that has the template with the `formControlName` directive that was passed a bad value (or a timing issue when the form control may not have yet been created by dynamically created forms)

Any information that may be useful for debugging is intentionally designed to be removed in production builds as to not impact the bundle size, so I don't think error messages can be improved in production.
Note that this is not a production build, but rather it is in production mode.
This is the same, the prod flag skips the debugging code (which is then removed by DCE).
After discussing it with the team, there is no consensus that this kind of debug info should land in the optimized bundle.

review_comments: I don't think `_throwError` is currently part of prod bundles, and the fact that this isn't detected in symbol tests could be because we may not have any coverage?
Yes, It would be great for our tests to cover this. Would you like this change in this PR or in a follow up ?
Wasn't Joost suggesting that this PR is broken, because `_throwError` will be missing from the bundle in prod? Or did I misunderstand?

He's talking about the symbol tests cf every `bundle.golden_symbols.json` if I'm not mistaken. 

@JoostK It looks like non-exported functions are not picked up by our symbol tests.
Fwiw In #47550, removing the error details was considered a problem.
Hm OK, that makes sense. I'm personally OK with the impact of adding the error in this case, since it's such a nuisance, but I'll leave the decision up to the two of you.

> Fwiw In #47550, removing the error details was considered a problem.

I agree with Kristiyan that retaining some form of error (potentially reduced in messaging verbosity) is beneficial _if_ that error may depend on potentially variable behavior depending on the environment; HTTP responses certainly fall into that bucket.

OTOH there's application bugs that may cause an app to fail, introducing technical errors such as the one reported in #57236. I'd argue to not sugar-coat those errors and save on bundle size overhead; production builds aren't designed to be helpful w.r.t. analyzing application bugs, that should be done using a development build where this error would have been nicely reported under the failing scenario (and the failing scenario isn't dependent on environmental behavior in this case).
